messages:

Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

Subject: Cirrus privacy ops: retention & ephemeral flag confirmation

Hi Ella / Tom,

Appreciate you carving out time today. Below is a concise recap of what we agreed and the concrete options we can include in your SOW for procurement/security to review. I've kept this intentionally short for your security ops folks.

Summary of your asks
- Clarify exactly what portions of prompt + model output are persisted by default, and for how long.
- Provide a per-request "ephemeral" option to prevent persistent storage and clarify support access procedures.
- Confirm embeddings handling when used for similarity search (managed vs. unmanaged).
- Provide US-only residency assurances and evidence for audits.

What Redwood currently supports (TL;DR)
- Default hosted retention: 30 days (request bodies + response text) in encrypted storage; can be changed to account-default 0 days at onboarding.
- Per-request opt-out: header no_persist=true available now; prevents writing to persistent logs.
- Embeddings: not stored by default unless you opt into managed indexing; unmanaged calls return vectors to you only.
- Dedicated/private: retention controlled by customer policy; private keeps data in your VPC/on-prem boundary.

PII controls we recommend for Cirrus
- Server-side redaction pipeline (we can drop common PHI patterns before logs) OR client-side redaction if you prefer full control.
- Hashing/pseudonymization for identifiers if you still need telemetry while protecting raw values.
- Deletion API + purge logs: we provide a deletion endpoint and can export confirmation logs as part of the SOW.

Attachments: redwood-retention-options-2024.csv (TTL vs. cost matrix) and SOC2-summary-2024.pdf (control scope).

Next actions for Cirrus
1) Please confirm the preferred account-default retention: 0 / 7 / 30 / 90 days.
2) Confirm whether you want server-side redaction (we can whitelist fields) or plan to redact client-side.
3) Share sec-ops@cirrushealth.com and legal@cirrushealth.com for document share.

I'll loop in Vivek to answer the more technical questions (headers, transient traces, support access). If helpful, we can convert the above into a one-paragraph SOW clause for procurement.

Cheers,
Tessa
Enterprise Solutions  Redwood Inference

Tessa,

Thanks for the helpful summary. A few clarifying questions our security team needs in writing before we open a formal review ticket:

1) Does the 30-day default include unredacted prompt text and full model responses? Are those stored in plaintext or encrypted at rest?
2) Is the no_persist=true header available today in production for hosted tenants? If so, does it prevent any access by Redwood support (including read-only debug access)?
3) If we call the embeddings API and then push vectors into our own vector store, does Redwood temporarily persist vectors for any period (for batching/throughput), or are they returned only and dropped?
4) For US-only residency: can you provide an attestation and a short list of the controls and procedures (backup retention, cross-region failover policy, employee access scope) we can attach to our security questionnaire?

Procurement note: please provide a short SOW clause or sentence we can drop into our procurement doc about retention and deletion.

sec-ops: sec-ops@cirrushealth.com
legal: legal@cirrushealth.com

Thanks,
Ella

Ella  quick answers and sample procurement language below. Happy to expand into a one-page artifact for your security questionnaire.

Answers:
1) Default 30-day logs: yes, that includes request body (prompt) and model output. Data is encrypted-at-rest with customer tenant keys where applicable; access is RBAC-protected and audited.
2) no_persist header: available now for hosted APIs. Requests marked no_persist are not written to persistent logs. Short-lived in-memory traces exist only for routing and are not accessible via support consoles. For replay-level debugging we require explicit, time-limited customer authorization which is logged.
3) Embeddings: by default we do NOT persist embeddings unless you enable our managed index. If you manage your own index, we do not write vectors to long-term storage. Transient buffering for throughput happens in memory and is not persisted.
4) US-only residency: we will provide a tenant attestation and a redacted on-call runbook showing access controls, KMS usage, and backup placement. We can also specify in SOW that backups and logs remain in US regions only.

Starter SOW clause (feel free to redline):
"Redwood will store Customer data, including request and response content, exclusively in United States regions, and will retain such data only for the Customer-specified retention period (0, 7, 30, or 90 days). Customer may employ per-request flags (for example, no_persist=true) to prevent persistent storage. Redwood shall provide a deletion API and will supply audit evidence of purge operations upon request. Support-level access to Customer data requires Customer authorization and is logged in audit records."

Action items:
- I will produce a concise redlined retention clause by EOD Monday and add it to the shared Drive link.
- Tessa  confirm Cirrus's choice of account-default retention so procurement can proceed (0 or 30 likely).
- Neha  attach SOC2 artifact and KMS notes to the Drive folder.

If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min walkthrough with sec-ops next week to answer any remaining questionnaire items.

Best,
